clue.text: Post that's got strings attached, just

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an ... is a vertical post, and an ... piano is one with strings attached
second meaning: ... as an adjective means honest and fair

explanation.walkthrough: The first stretch reads like a job offer with conditions; it describes an upright, the post-like piano whose strings run vertically.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright piano stands like a post and is strung; as an adjective, a just person is honourable and principled.

clue.text: Extract idiot blocking attendant

indicators.note: the idiot sits inside the attendant, blocking the way through him

parts.note: a page is a young attendant
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a fool out of the way of a servant who is being obstructed.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is an extract or excerpt taken from a longer piece of writing or music.

clue.text: Dialect used by papers on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on top of another comes first

parts.note: ID, identity documents, are one's papers
IOM is the standard abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A local form of speech appears in the newspapers printed on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is the particular form of speech of a people or region, close to a dialect.

clue.text: Head office girl's soaring cry of adoration

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising upward means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: Anna's, a girl's name with the possessive

explanation.surface: A woman at corporate headquarters lets out a high-pitched shout of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosanna is a shout of praise and worship to God, used in hymns and liturgy.

clue.text: Picks priest to replace lead in Greek play

indicators.note: the priest's letter takes the place of the first letter of the play's title

parts.note: Electra is a tragedy by Sophocles, and another by Euripides

explanation.surface: A director chooses a clergyman to take over the leading role in a Greek tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Plectra, plural of plectrum, are the small flat tools used to pluck guitar strings.

clue.text: London theatre's Gilbert's work

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Lyric is a West End theatre on Shaftesbury Avenue
second meaning: W. S. Gilbert wrote the words of the songs in the Savoy operas

explanation.walkthrough: Read the first two words as the possessive of the Lyric, a West End theatre; the apostrophe is ignored, as is the crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert supplied the words of the songs while Sullivan wrote the music, so his contribution was the song texts.

clue.text: He can't possibly employ singer

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of he can't may be arranged in another way

parts.note: to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: A man protests that he could not possibly hire a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A chanteuse is a female singer, especially of popular songs in a nightclub or cabaret.

clue.text: Screens rare violins fellow's left

indicators.note: the fellow has left, so his letter departs from the violins

parts.note: fiddles is an informal word for violins
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS; the fellow is the one who has left

explanation.surface: An auditioning panel screens rare violins after one of the players has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a coarse sieve, so to riddle earth or gravel is to sift it; screens is a synonym.

clue.text: Trained choir with acolytes?

indicators.note: trained means the letters of choir and acolytes are put into new order

explanation.surface: A rehearsed church choir sings alongside the altar servers.
explanation.definitionFit: A choral society is an amateur organisation of singers, the sort of trained choir the whole clue pictures.

clue.text: Drink at the start of 'As Time Goes By'

indicators.note: the letters sit at the very start of the song title's words

explanation.surface: A drink is poured at the opening bars of the song from Casablanca.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian white wine from Piedmont, so a drink.

clue.text: Playful style to some ears avoids D in a number

indicators.note: to some ears means the word is said aloud and only roughly matched

parts.note: to skirt is to avoid, so skirts means avoids

indicators.note: the letter D goes inside the a and number pair

explanation.surface: A musical piece avoids the note D in one number, giving a lighter feel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian-looking start, said aloud, comes near the English word skirts.
explanation.definitionFit: Scherzando is a musical direction meaning to play in a light, jesting manner, a playful style.

clue.text: French city maintains empty room for opera

indicators.note: the city holds and keeps the room's letters within it

parts.note: Caen is a city in Normandy

indicators.note: emptying the room removes its inside letters, leaving its first and last

explanation.surface: A city in France keeps an unused room ready for staging an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmen is Bizet's opera about a Seville cigarette girl, first staged in 1875.

clue.text: Article's pulled apart performances

indicators.note: pulled apart means the letters of article's are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A critic's newspaper article tears some concerts to shreds.
explanation.definitionFit: Recitals are concerts given by a solo performer or small group, so musical performances.

clue.text: Note crowd's half-hearted version of 'Unforgettable'

parts.note: a memo is a written note

indicators.note: the doubled letter at the crowd's heart is halved, losing one of the pair

parts.note: a rabble is a disorderly crowd

explanation.surface: A rowdy audience gives a lacklustre rendition of the Nat King Cole song.
explanation.definitionFit: Memorable is a synonym, another version of the word unforgettable: something not easily forgotten.

clue.text: Approaches green river with very large banks

indicators.note: the very large letters form the banks either side of the rest

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, very large
vert is green in heraldry
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone approaches an unspoilt river flanked by very high banks.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtures are first moves or friendly advances towards someone, so approaches made to them.

clue.text: Rhythm builds regularly during exercises

indicators.note: the picked letters come during the exercises, sitting inside them

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of builds

explanation.surface: A steady beat develops as a workout goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is a regular beat or throb, so a rhythm, in music as in the heart.

clue.text: Printed music, sweet stuff, excludes R&B

indicators.note: excludes means the two letters are left out of the sweet

parts.note: sherbet is a fizzy powdered sweet
the letters R and B, also rhythm and blues

explanation.surface: A sweet sort of score leaves out rhythm and blues.
explanation.walkthrough: R&B reads as the music genre but just supplies the two letters R and B.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheet music is music printed on loose pages, so a printed copy of a piece.

clue.text: Repeated refrain from small miners? Who cares?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the marching song of the seven dwarfs, who mine in Disney's Snow White
second meaning: an exclamation of weary resignation

explanation.walkthrough: The small miners are the seven dwarfs of Disney's Snow White, whose work song repeats the refrain.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both the dwarfs' song chorus and a sigh expressing boredom or indifference.

clue.text: Composer zoned out with a couple of Italians

indicators.note: out means zoned and the two pieces are put in a different order

parts.note: IT is an abbreviation for Italian, taken twice

explanation.surface: A musician drifts off in the company of two people from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaetano Donizetti was the Italian composer of operas such as Lucia di Lammermoor.

clue.text: Sang dully in key, including bum note

indicators.note: the reworked note goes between in and the key letter

parts.note: D is a musical key

indicators.note: bum in the sense of wrong or bad tells us note is rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer stays in key but hits one wrong note in a flat performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To intone is to chant on a single monotonous pitch, so sang dully fits the past tense.

clue.text: Tinker with tempo primarily, then go

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter of tempo

parts.note: widdle is British slang for urinate, as in needing to go

explanation.surface: Someone fiddles with the musical speed first, then moves on.
explanation.walkthrough: Go here is the informal sense of going to the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To twiddle is to fiddle idly or adjust something aimlessly, so to tinker with it.

clue.text: Current English sailors support their bosses

indicators.note: in a down clue, the supporting pieces sit underneath the other

parts.note: the MOD, Ministry of Defence, runs the armed forces
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: Naval men in England back their senior officers in a present-day matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means of the present time, up to date, which is what current means as an adjective.

clue.text: Backing group of Verdi's outrivalled top players

indicators.note: backing means the letters found are read from right to left
a group of consecutive letters is taken from Verdi's outrivalled

explanation.surface: A band accompanying a Verdi singer outshone the star performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtuosi are performers of outstanding technical skill, especially musicians: the best players.

clue.text: Head back with a German to find station

indicators.note: back means the word for head is reversed

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: A German heads home to locate a railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: To tune in is to set a radio to receive a particular broadcasting station.

clue.text: Attack revolutionary symbols in bars

indicators.note: turning round, as in a revolution, sends the phrase backwards

parts.note: to set on someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: A rebel group launches an assault on symbols displayed in pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Bars here are musical measures, not pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical notes are the written signs placed on a stave within each measure of a score.

clue.text: State capital's nifty footwork

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the capital of West Virginia
second meaning: the lively 1920s dance with kicking steps

explanation.definitionFit: The city in West Virginia shares its name with the Jazz Age dance known for quick kicks and swivels.

clue.text: Arrange silly ditty, sacrificing a tango

indicators.note: silly signals the remaining letters are jumbled
sacrificing means giving up the tango letter from ditty

parts.note: taken as written; the answer also runs backwards across silly ditty, but that is a coincidence: the parse is the deletion and anagram
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A musician sets out a foolish little song, dropping a tango from it.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the T from DITTY leaves DITY, and 'silly' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy is to put things in order, the sense of arrange as in arranging a room.

clue.text: Note expert's very big error in Rhode Island

indicators.note: the outsize mistake goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island
OS stands for outsize
a sin is a wrong or error

explanation.surface: A specialist commits a huge blunder while in Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Rossini, composer of The Barber of Seville, was a master of musical notes, a cryptic way of naming a composer.

clue.text: Poem about heart of Ulysses with happy ending

definitions.text: Poem about heart of Ulysses with happy ending

indicators.note: the poem goes around the central letters

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

indicators.note: the heart is the central letters of Ulysses
ending means the last letter of happy

explanation.surface: Homer's epic centres on Ulysses and finishes happily with his homecoming.
explanation.definitionFit: The Odyssey is Homer's epic about Ulysses' long voyage home, ending in reunion with Penelope.
